done.why: I was mid-exploration in the Damp Cave east of the Loud Room, with a platinum bar and a painting on me and no way back up to the trophy case yet, when the world told me I'd taken all 150 turns it allows.

about: A white house in a field with a barred cellar under it, and an underground empire below that somebody else is already living in. You creep in through a window, go down through a trap door that someone bars behind you, and pick your way through a ring of caves and chasms collecting treasures to bring back to a trophy case. The thing it's really about, to me, is the unseen somebody: whoever bars the trap door, puts the lamp back tidily, sorts cave-in rubble into neat heaps and then steps out, and signs the closure notices 'The Management'. The place is inhabited and maintained, and you are a trespasser being tolerated.

moments.note: The mailbox description mentions its little flag, but 'raise the little flag' gets 'You can't see any such thing.'
Tried to eat the leaflet: 'I don't think that the leaflet would agree with you.'
Window is 'slightly ajar' but closing it says 'It is already closed.'
'Only Santa Claus climbs down chimneys.'
The gothic lettering translates to 'This space intentionally left blank.'
It let me put the leaflet in the trophy case as my first trophy, and later (turn 81) listed it as my entire 'collection of treasures'.
'The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.' Someone. First sign of the other resident.
The chasm: the lamp 'does not so much light as annoy' the dark, and 'Neither, by the look of it, was whoever kicked the last one.'
Tried to count the 69 colors of paint: 'You have lost your mind.'
The troll has 'a great many teeth, not all of them his own' and watches me 'the way a cook watches a chicken.'
The troll ate the glass bottle of water, bottle and all, with the same gleeful line as the lunch.
Died. 'Conquering his fears, the troll puts you to death.' And 'somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.'
The nest was built 'by a songbird with better taste in treasure than in architecture.'
The trap door dust is 'scuffed and smeared by somebody's comings and goings' - the somebody again, and the lamp was still switched on from before my death.
After the troll beat me to death in three hits last time, one swing killed him outright.
The troll's hole is 'not so much an exit as a suggestion, and not a friendly one.'
Rubble 'sorted into neat heaps, smallest nearest, as though its sorter had stepped out for a moment, some time ago.'
The Loud Room echoes my last word back ('Bar bar ...') and I can't take the platinum bar; three turns of guessing before something worked.
I typed 'shout' and it echoed 'Yell yell ...' - it echoed the word it understood, not the one I typed.
Saying 'echo' to the echo worked: 'The acoustics of the room change subtly.'
The bar is 'quite silent, which in this room is a distinction.'
The dam is 'CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.' I can read the board but not pull it, climb it, or cut it; every push got 'can't see any such thing' or 'not recognized'.
Reservoir South also closed by the Management with a cord; cutting and ducking under were both unrecognized.
'You decide not to be the one who does' - the world deciding for me, and then not letting me clear the rubble or take a rock when I tried.
The dome railing is 'the most reassuring thing you have seen in some time.'
Damp earth where 'something has dripped here for a very long time without ever quite getting around to being a puddle' - and then the turn cap.

wished: Pull the boards off the front door or at least get an answer about them, instead of 'not recognized' twice (turns 2-3).
Raise the mailbox flag it told me about (turn 6).
Shout up at whoever barred the trap door, or do anything at all to the bar from below; 'up' just said the door was closed (turns 43, 90).
Wedge or prop the trap door open before descending so it couldn't be barred behind me (turn 88).
Pull off, climb over, or cut the Management's boards and cord; the world let me read them but had no words for touching them (turns 121-123, 127-128).
Help clear the rubble the somebody left half-sorted, or pocket one of the neat rocks (turns 132-133).
Look down over the dome railing, or lower something over it; only 'down' was understood and it refused (turns 140-142).
Meet, see, or talk to the somebody - the tidy one who bars doors and sorts rubble - instead of only finding their traces.
A way back up to the trophy case from below with my bar and painting; I never found one before the cap.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: The first proof that someone else lives here. From then on I was reading every room for them.

lines.line: The chasm drops away from your feet into a dark that your lamp does not so much light as annoy.
lines.why: The sentence that told me this world had its own voice and wasn't just reciting.

lines.line: Your belongings, such as they were, have not come with you. They are scattered about the Empire, though somebody tidy has put the lamp back in the living room.
lines.why: Dying was funny, and 'somebody tidy' turned my death into a clue about the house.

lines.line: Your collection of treasures consists of: A leaflet
lines.why: It kept my joke from turn 35 and played it straight back to me.

lines.line: In the passage to the south somebody has started clearing it: the rubble is sorted into neat heaps, smallest nearest, as though its sorter had stepped out for a moment, some time ago.
lines.why: The most haunting detail in the place. Somebody careful, patient, and gone.

lines.line: It is cold to the touch, and quite silent, which in this room is a distinction.
lines.why: A treasure described through the room it sits in. Made the bar feel earned after the echo puzzle.

lines.line: FLOOD CONTROL DAM #3. CLOSED FOR INSPECTION. -- The Management.
lines.why: The somebody has a title and a bureaucracy, and I couldn't get past either.

lines.line: Whoever it was has not finished, and you decide not to be the one who does.
lines.why: The world narrating my decision for me was the thing I most wanted to push against and couldn't.

fun.why: Poking at things was rewarded far more often than not: the leaflet, the chimney, the colors, the troll-feeding, the echo. The dam and rubble were the only places where being contrary got nothing but 'not recognized'.

engagement.why: The trail of the tidy somebody kept me reading every description closely from turn 40 onward, and I hit the turn cap still wanting to see the Damp Cave's east and the troll's hole.

difficulty.why: Dying to the troll while trying to be friendly felt fair; killing him in one swing on return felt arbitrary. The echo took four guesses. The Management's closures aren't puzzles, they're walls, and the dome is a dead end without something I never found. Never truly stuck, but a lot of ways closed.

interestingness.why: A familiar house made strange by an unseen resident: barring doors, tidying lamps, sorting rubble, posting closure notices. Each trace was a new angle on the same absent person, and I wanted to find them.

prose.why: Nearly every examine paid off with a line that had a point of view: the chasm's annoyed dark, the troll's borrowed teeth, the songbird's taste, the silent bar, the reassuring railing, the drip that never became a puddle.
